{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the fish's tail, the round loop that makes the outline read as a fish and not just an oval. I laid it by tracing stroke 3 from the shared sketch. It branches off the body at the crossing, and I closed the loop back toward the belly. By our last check, about 108 of the 111 standing dominoes were connected to the start, and the tail was part of that run.

Execution: I started the tail early and waited until the body lines reached the crossing so it would pick up the fall. Later I did two close inspections to look for breaks, and I stood one domino back up. I kept my hands off the nose and middle crossing once the team asked, which avoided bump risk in the areas others were working.

Collaboration: I backed the fish idea straight away so the table could start building. I took the stroke Sofia assigned me and kept the group posted on tail progress. I also flagged the small sideways offset I saw at the middle crossing and left it to Sofia, who owned that area. I stayed away from the nose so I wouldn't bump Hana while she worked there.

Leadership: I kept the table's energy up through the build, with regular updates and encouragement, and I stayed in the shared hands-off agreement as the push approached. I took clear ownership of one piece of the picture, finished it, and then moved to checking the shared work.", "my_share_percent": 28}
